t: You are at Wesley's Chapel, in St Luke's, the southern part of Islington. It opened in 1778 and was built under the direction of John Wesley, founder of the Methodist movement. George Dance the Younger designed it. People call it the Mother Church of World Methodism. It is still a place of worship, and the Museum of Methodism is in the crypt, with John Wesley's House next door. Wesley himself is buried here. So is Jabez Bunting, the most prominent Methodist after Wesley's death. The poet Agnes Bulmer, who wrote a very long epic called Messiah's Kingdom, is also buried here.
